title: Landing page vs. the bar
subtitle: Skills Board's homepage, rebuilt piece by piece and judged blind against Linear, Vercel and input-otp.rodz.dev. A builder and an independent critic work each piece; the critic never knows which screenshot is ours.

notes.text: Session opened. Dependencies installed, dev server up on :3000, baseline screenshots captured at 1440x900 and 390x844.
Reference capture blocked: egress policy refused CONNECT to all three reference hosts. Raised with Tommaso.
Egress opened. Chromium's own TLS to the proxy still resets, so captures now route every request through Node's proxy-aware fetch and fulfil it into the page.
All three references captured full-page, desktop and mobile, into refs/.
Refactor in flight: splitting the 708-line page and 1703-line CSS module into per-section files so builders can work in parallel without collisions. Must come out pixel-identical.
Motion recon in flight: driving input-otp.rodz.dev live to extract its real timing, easing and interruptibility behaviour into a written spec.
Refactor landed: 62 screenshot pairs byte-identical across both flag permutations, both themes and reduced motion. Committed and pushed.
Art direction in flight. Seven builders working separately would produce seven aesthetics, so one director derives a shared spec from the references first.
Round 0 judging: three critics comparing our current page blind against each reference. Each sees two unlabelled screenshots and must pick one.
Round 0 result: we beat Vercel and input-otp on static composition, and lost to Linear. Critics were unanimous on why — Linear's page carries real product evidence on every screen; ours pads.

Three independent critics, none of whom saw the other two, all named the same defect: the empty run after the hero, the ghost-text MCP column, and the giant outlined 0. That is the structural verdict, not a style note.
Mobile judged. Same split as desktop: we beat Vercel and input-otp, we lose to Linear. Standing is 4-2.
Both losses are to the same page for the same reason. Linear re-composes for each viewport and puts real product evidence on every screen; we stack one layout and pad the gaps.
New mobile-specific defect, named by two critics independently: the hero card cluster is an illegible shrunken collage at 390px and wastes the first scroll.

Art direction delivered. It measured what the critics only felt: 4094px of our 7006px page — 58% — is uniform empty ground, and the cause is two sticky runways totalling 220vh that produce no new content by construction.
Page recomposed: chapter rail deleted, and two new sections wired in — a proof strip under the fold and a product slab before the MCP section.

Shared type and layout ramp added: ten steps on desktop collapsing to seven below 1024px. The page currently renders 33 distinct type combinations from seven different vw slopes. Builders now apply the ramp instead of inventing sizes.
Eight builders out in parallel, each owning its own files. Critics follow once they land.

pieces.name: Whole page
pieces.scope: The page as one object: rhythm, length, whether every screen of scroll earns itself.

rounds.why: Ours commits to one system — off-white ground, a single green used sparingly, hairline rules, a tight scale; Vercel read as unrelated panels with no shared grid.
Ours reads as one editorial system at a confident display scale; input-otp read as a stack of dark modules at near-identical spacing with no rhythm change.
Linear sustains one repeated module with dense real product imagery, so every screen of scroll delivers new evidence rather than new layout ideas.

pieces.gap: Dead vertical space and unresolved sections. All three critics named it independently, including both we beat: a near-empty viewport after the hero, an MCP third column of grey ghost text, and a black band holding a giant outlined 0 that reads as placeholder art.

pieces.name: Evidence
pieces.scope: Two new sections: a proof strip under the fold, and a product slab showing the library itself.
pieces.gap: This is the piece we actually lost on. Linear carries real product surface in every module; we showed the product nowhere.

pieces.name: Hero
pieces.scope: Headline type, eyebrow, subcopy, CTA cluster, the dossier board, entrance choreography, sticky exit.

pieces.name: Chrome
pieces.scope: Sticky header, scroll progress, chapter rail, footer colophon.

pieces.name: Workflow
pieces.scope: The three-move sequence and its section head.

pieces.name: MCP
pieces.scope: Sticky chapter, copy column, the routing schematic and its animation.

pieces.name: Pricing
pieces.scope: The zero monument and the Free Forever statement.

pieces.name: FAQ + closing
pieces.scope: Disclosure list, closing statement, final call to action.

pieces.name: Motion system
pieces.scope: Springs, interruptibility, hover and press feedback, scroll timing, reduced-motion.

pieces.name: Mobile
pieces.scope: Every section at 390px, judged on its own terms.

rounds.why: Ours reads as composed for 390px — full-width hero, two-tone headline at a genuinely mobile scale, stacked CTAs, thumb-sized accordion rows; Vercel shrank a desktop layout until its feature lists hit 5-6px.
Our type scale was re-set for the narrow column with real leading and 24px edge margins; input-otp shipped 8-10px body text and a 21,700px scroll.
Linear re-composes for the column — full-bleed visuals using the entire width, one visual and one sentence per section; ours stacks the desktop layout into a card column.

pieces.gap: The hero card cluster is illegible at 390px. Two critics called it independently: a shrunken collage that wastes the first scroll, with text too small to parse. Mobile type hierarchy is also flat — headings, eyebrows and body sit at near-identical weight and size.
